T1.implementation_approach: Organize the project into folders for backend, frontend, and shared resources. Use a framework or boilerplate for initial setup.
T1.notes: Ensure proper version control with Git and set up environment variables.

T2.implementation_approach: Identify entities and relationships, create ER diagrams, and translate them into tables with appropriate keys and constraints.
T2.notes: Normalize the database to avoid redundancy and ensure scalability.

T3.implementation_approach: Implement user registration and login using hashed passwords and JWT for session management.
T3.notes: Ensure secure password storage and implement rate limiting to prevent brute force attacks.

T4.implementation_approach: Create RESTful APIs to manage problems, including CRUD operations for problem data.
T4.notes: Implement validation and error handling for API endpoints.

T5.implementation_approach: Develop a code editor using a library like Monaco Editor and integrate it with the backend.
T5.notes: Ensure syntax highlighting and real-time updates in the editor.

T6.implementation_approach: Create a system to execute user-submitted code in a secure sandbox environment and return results.
T6.notes: Ensure security by isolating code execution and limiting resource usage.

T7.implementation_approach: Develop APIs to manage user profiles, including updating details and viewing progress.
T7.notes: Include features like profile picture upload and activity tracking.

T8.implementation_approach: Create APIs to fetch and update leaderboard data based on user performance.
T8.notes: Optimize queries for real-time leaderboard updates.

T9.implementation_approach: Develop a user interface to display and filter problems from the repository.
T9.notes: Ensure responsive design and efficient search functionality.

T10.implementation_approach: Create a user interface to display the leaderboard with sorting and filtering options.
T10.notes: Ensure real-time updates and a visually appealing design.

T11.implementation_approach: Connect the code editor frontend with the backend to send code for execution and display results.
T11.notes: Handle asynchronous communication and error scenarios effectively.

T12.implementation_approach: Write unit and integration tests for authentication APIs using a testing framework.
T12.notes: Test for edge cases like invalid credentials and expired tokens.

T13.implementation_approach: Simulate code submissions and verify the correctness and performance of the online judge system.
T13.notes: Include tests for security and resource limits.

T14.implementation_approach: Deploy the application using a cloud platform and set up CI/CD pipelines for automated deployment.
T14.notes: Ensure scalability and monitor application performance post-deployment.

from flask_sqlalchemy import SQLAlchemy

db = SQLAlchemy()

from app.database import db

class Problem:
    def __init__(self, id, title, description, difficulty, tags=None):
        """
        Initialize a Problem instance.

        :param id: Unique identifier for the problem
        :param title: Title of the problem
        :param description: Detailed description of the problem
        :param difficulty: Difficulty level of the problem (e.g., 'Easy', 'Medium', 'Hard')
        :param tags: Optional list of tags associated with the problem
        """
        self.id = id
        self.title = title
        self.description = description
        self.difficulty = difficulty
        self.tags = tags or []

    def to_dict(self):
        """
        Convert the Problem instance to a dictionary.

        :return: Dictionary representation of the problem
        """
        return {
            'id': self.id,
            'title': self.title,
            'description': self.description,
            'difficulty': self.difficulty,
            'tags': self.tags
        }

from app.controllers.problem_controller import problem_bp
from app.controllers.user_controller import user_bp
from app.controllers.solution_controller import solution_bp

def register_blueprints(app):
    app.register_blueprint(problem_bp)
    app.register_blueprint(user_bp)
    app.register_blueprint(solution_bp)

from flask import Flask, render_template
from app.database import db
from app.routes import register_blueprints

def create_app():
    # Initialize Flask app
    app = Flask(__name__)

    # Configure database
    app.config['SQLALCHEMY_DATABASE_URI'] = 'sqlite:///app.db'
    app.config['SQLALCHEMY_TRACK_MODIFICATIONS'] = False
    
    # Initialize database
    db.init_app(app)

    # Register blueprints
    register_blueprints(app)

    # Define a default route
    @app.route('/')
    def index():
        return render_template('index.html')

    return app

from app import create_app

if __name__ == "__main__":
    app = create_app()
    app.run()

code_repository.readme_content:
# ACM Problem-Solving Platform

A web application designed to help users practice and solve ACM-style competitive programming problems.

## Features

- Problem Repository: A comprehensive library of ACM-style problems categorized by difficulty and topic.
- Code Editor: An integrated code editor with support for multiple programming languages and syntax highlighting.
- Online Judge System: An automated system to evaluate code submissions and provide real-time feedback on correctness and performance.
- User Profiles: Personalized user accounts to track progress, view solved problems, and maintain a history of submissions.
- Leaderboard: A ranking system to display top performers and encourage competition among users.

## Setup

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
python app.py
```

## Usage

Open http://localhost:5000 in your browser.
